# Language

The syntax and keywords of the language, which is the same in BlitzBasic, Blitz3D and BlitzPlus. Commands such as `Print`, `Rect` or `CreateCube` are in the [[Command-Index]], this page is about what the compiler understands by itself. Keywords and names are not case sensitive, and `;` starts a comment that lasts to the end of the line.

## Variables and types

A variable has one of three types, which a suffix on its name says: `%` is an integer (also the default), `#` a float, `$` a string. Variables you assign to are created on first use. `Local` makes a variable that only exists in its function, `Global` makes one that every function can see, and `Const` makes a name for a value that cannot change.

```blitzbasic
Const LIMIT = 3
Global total% = 0
For i = 1 To LIMIT
	total = total + i
Next
half# = total / 2.0
name$ = "sum"
Print name$ + " " + total + " " + half#
```

```text
sum 6 3.0
```

`Int`, `Float` and `Str` convert between the types (`Int` rounds to the nearest whole number), and `Handle` and `Object` convert between an object and a number that stands for it.

```blitzbasic
Print Int(3.7)
Print Float(2) / 4
Print Str(12) + "!"
```

```text
4
0.5
12!
```

## Operators

| Operators | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+ - * / ^` | Arithmetic. Dividing two integers gives an integer, so use a float to get a fraction. |
| `Mod` | Remainder of a division. |
| `Shl Shr Sar` | Shift bits left, right, and right keeping the sign. |
| `And Or Xor Not` | Bitwise and logical operators. |
| `= <> < > <= >=` | Comparison. They give 1 for true and 0 for false. |
| `Abs() Sgn() Pi` | Absolute value, sign (-1, 0 or 1) and the number 3.14159. |

```blitzbasic
Print 7 Mod 4
Print 1 Shl 4
Print -8 Sar 1
Print 5 Xor 1
Print Abs(-3)
Print Sgn(-2)
```

```text
3
16
-4
4
3
-1
```

## Control flow

```blitzbasic
x = 2
If x = 1
	Print "one"
ElseIf x = 2
	Print "two"
Else
	Print "many"
EndIf

Select x
	Case 1 : Print "case one"
	Case 2, 3 : Print "case two or three"
	Default : Print "default"
End Select

For i = 10 To 1 Step -4
	Print i
Next

While x < 4
	x = x + 1
Wend

Repeat
	x = x - 1
Until x <= 2
Print x
```

```text
two
case two or three
10
6
2
2
```

`Exit` leaves the closest loop, `Repeat ... Forever` loops until `Exit`, `Goto` jumps to a `.label`, and `Gosub` calls the code at a label that ends with `Return`.

## Functions

```blitzbasic
Function Double(n)
	Return n * 2
End Function

Function Greet$(name$, loud = 0)
	If loud Then Return Upper$(name$) + "!"
	Return name$
End Function

Print Double(21)
Print Greet$("hi")
Print Greet$("hi", 1)
```

```text
42
hi
HI!
```

A suffix after the function name says what type it returns, and a parameter with `= value` is optional.

## Arrays

`Dim` makes an array whose indices go from 0 up to the number you give, so `Dim a(3)` has four elements.

```blitzbasic
Dim a(3)
a(2) = 5
Print a(2)
Dim grid(2, 2)
grid(1, 2) = 9
Print grid(1, 2)
```

```text
5
9
```

## Types

A `Type` describes a record with fields. `New` creates one, `Delete` removes it, and `\` reads a field. Every type keeps a list of its objects, which `First`, `Last`, `Before`, `After` and `For ... Each` walk through, and `Insert` moves an object inside that list.

```blitzbasic
Type Point
	Field x, y
End Type

For i = 1 To 3
	p.Point = New Point
	p\x = i
Next

For p.Point = Each Point
	Print p\x
Next

Delete First Point
l.Point = Last Point
Print l\x
```

```text
1
2
3
3
```

## Data

`Data` holds values in the program, `Read` takes the next one, and `Restore` goes back to a label.

```blitzbasic
Restore numbers
Read a
Read b
Print a + b
.numbers
Data 3, 4
```

```text
7
```

## Other keywords

`Include "file.bb"` puts another source file in this place, `True` and `False` are 1 and 0, `Null` is the empty object, and `End` stops the program.
